title: Localization Hom and multiplication tower criterion
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site with small underlying category, let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal C$, let $f\in\mathcal O(U)$, and let $K\in D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. On the slice site $\mathcal C/U$, let $T(K|_U,f)$ be a derived inverse limit [def-weil-derived-limit] in $D(\mathcal O_U)$ of the tower $\cdots\xrightarrow{f}K|_U\xrightarrow{f}K|_U$ whose transition maps are multiplication by $f$ [def-weil-inverse-system]. Then $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U[1/f],K|_U)=0$ if and only if $T(K|_U,f)=0$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom].

proof.text: On the slice, use the coefficient localization as the colimit of the repeated multiplication sequence from its definition. The existing generic theorem `CategoryTheory.telescope_shortExact` in `Sheaf.RingTheory.ModuleLocalizationTowerVanishing` supplies the short exact sequence for the telescope; its monicity hypothesis is discharged by the sequential telescope monomorphism theorem in the Grothendieck abelian category of slice module sheaves.

proof.text: In a distinguished triangle the first object is zero if and only if its second morphism is invertible. Apply this both to the dualized telescope triangle and to the triangle supplied by the hypothesis that T is a derived limit. Conjugation by the product isomorphism preserves invertibility, so the two zero conditions are equivalent. No uniqueness theorem for derived limits is used.
